title: Avoiding War
text: That Trash and that Crimson Swine glaring at me and my Father, along with Itsuki and the soldiers of the nation. Well… what should we do? They may be the insolent fools trying to set a trap for my Father, but if we act rashly, it could lead to war. Then we’d be right back where we started.
“Father, please don’t despair. You are not alone. Even if the whole world turns against you, I, Motoyasu, will stand by your side.”
“K-Kitamura-kun…?”
I help my father to his feet, then glare at the Trash.
“How ridiculous.”
Just then, Ren calmly—and seemingly disinterested—begins to walk away from the throne room.
“Ren-san! What do you mean by that?”

“I just thought Motoyasu had a point… Even if she’s a princess, there’s a limit to punishing Naofumi based on the testimony of a single woman. Watching yesterday’s exchange, it looked like the people in the castle were just going through the motions of something that had already been decided from the start.”
My Father stared blankly at Ren and me.

“Don’t get me wrong. I’m not saying Naofumi is right. Still, it’s a fact that the Shield Hero is weak, and when Motoyasu tries to be kind to Naofumi only to be cut off every time, it’s natural to start having doubts.”
“Grr…”
“Boo-boo! Boo-boo-boo-boo-boo!”

The Crimson Swine points at my Father while squealing something. Then, it seemed to be pleading with Itsuki and Ren. Itsuki looked at his Father, his anger plain to see, while Ren simply stared impassively.
“I didn’t do it!”
“…Either way, we don’t have enough evidence to punish Naofumi. If you want to make a scene, go ahead and do it on your own. It’s a waste of time. Don’t call us over for such trivial matters.”
Looking displeased, Ren walked away. His companions followed after him.
“Bububububu!”

The Crimson Swine is squealing, isn’t it? Is it losing its temper because things aren’t going its way? I suppose it’s revealed its true form. What an ugly, truly hideous sight. I can’t let my Father look at such a vulgar creature for much longer.
“Come, Father, let’s get out of here. It’s pointless to say anything here.”
Taking Father’s hand, we leave the throne room.
“Ah… yeah.”

Ren, who had been half-convinced and half-skeptical throughout the exchange, seems to have vaguely sensed which side is at fault. It’s a positive sign, but I also sense a bit of danger. The fact remains that if we don’t move cautiously, Ren could very well be assassinated. Well, knowing Ren as I do… let’s just assume there won’t be any problems yet.
On our way out of the castle, the soldiers glared at us with displeasure, but when I glared back, they quickly looked away.
“Um… thanks for saving me, Kitamura… I mean, Motoyasu Kitamura.”
“It’s no big deal. I just trust my Father.”
“Yeah… I didn’t do it. I didn’t drink any sake yesterday; I was just resting at the inn.”

I talk with my father, who’s wearing just his undershirt, in the town square. This has happened before, hasn’t it? Was I actually able to save my father? I can’t help but worry that by taking his side, I might actually be putting his life in even greater danger.
“Motoyasu-kun?”
“I’d like to talk to you somewhere private for a moment.”
“Huh? Uh… sure. It’s fine—I can’t fight on my own anyway.”
“That’s true. And while we’re at it… we should get some clothes. I know you’re not alone, after all.”
To make him look as weak as possible, it might be best to have Father wear clothes that look cheap.
“Where are we going?”
“You can’t go out in just your undershirt. We’re going to buy some gear right now. Don’t worry—I’ll cover the cost.”
“I’ve got money, so it’s fine!”

Huh? Unlike the time before last, does my Father actually have money this time? He reaches inside his shield and shows me a silver coin. This is… I’m pretty sure he threw a silver coin at me back in the first world. That’s the same coin. I take my hat off to my Father’s foresight—he’s really covering all his bases.
“Motoyasu-kun. W-why are you crying?”
“There are all sorts of reasons, you know. Come on, let’s go! We’re going to buy armor for Father.”
“U-uh-huh.”
And so, I stopped by the weapons shop—which had opened early that morning—that Father apparently frequented.
The exchange after we entered the shop wasn’t much different from the one two episodes ago. The shopkeeper approached Father and, based on his character, decided to trust him.
“So? What are you going to wear, An-chan?”
“Before that, I’d like to talk to my Father—even if it’s just in the back of the shop.”
“Hm? Well, all right…”
The shopkeeper kindly led us to the back of the shop. Then, he set up a chair for us in the back room.
“Come out front once you’re done talking.”
The shopkeeper thoughtfully excused himself and left.
“What’s the matter, Motoyasu-kun?”
“First, I’d like to explain the situation to you—how to enhance our weapons and our plan moving forward.”
“Huh? Ah… yeah.”
My Father nodded, looking completely bewildered.
“First, I need to discuss something important with you.”
“What? The story about looping back from the future… I find that hard to believe on the spot.”
“It’s the truth, you know.”
“Then! Why didn’t you tell me I’d be framed for a crime I didn’t commit!?”
My Father came at me, practically shouting. I… took the full brunt of his anger.

“Well… I’m sorry. In the last loop, I told you right after I was summoned. I told you that I’d set a trap for you and drive you out penniless… and then, regarding the country’s situation… I explained that the Shield Hero is a hero worshipped in a nation hostile to this country, Melromarc.”
“Huh?”

My father stood there, completely dumbfounded. Come to think of it, that’s true. At this point, he doesn’t know that Melromarc is a human nation that discriminates against Demi-Humans. And there’s no way he could have known that the Demi-Humans worship the Shield Hero, either.
“Why didn’t you tell me!”
“There’s more to this story… On the very night you made such a fuss… I was ambushed at the castle, and Father was tricked into getting into a carriage and taken away.”
“When I finally managed to catch up, Father was on the verge of being killed by Melromarc’s soldiers. That’s what happened on the very first day after I was summoned.”

“The first day… Hmm, now that I think about it, Motoyasu-kun has been looking out for me from the very beginning. Even when I couldn’t make any friends, he tried to push his own companions onto me… He tried to teach me how to enhance my weapons and how to get stronger, too. So there was a reason he looked so uncomfortable when that woman was talking to me so familiarly.”
Just as I expected from my Father. You figured out everything from just what I said. Still, “women,” huh?
“Those are pigs.”
“Pigs…?”
“Pigs are pigs. They’re despicable lifeforms who put themselves first, think only of using others, and discard them like trash once they’re done.”
“Ah… yeah. I kind of get why Motoyasu-kun calls women pigs now. So?”
“Starting the very next day, assassins began coming for you regularly, Father, and we accepted the invitation from the envoys of Siltvelt—a nation of Demi-Humans who worship you—and set out.”

I went on to explain the events of our previous journey to my father in detail. How we crossed the border fortress, how we defeated the assassins, and how the town we stopped at was attacked. It was a short journey, but a lot happened.
“So…? What did I do once I arrived in the kingdom of Siltvelt? Did I try to take revenge on that country or something?”
“My Father didn’t do anything like that. He let it go, saying there were people who believed in him.”
“…That’s amazing. Well, I’m feeling pretty much the same way right now… If anything, I’d rather have nothing to do with those guys at all.”
“The first time the loop happened, I protected my Father just like this. Back then, to ensure Father’s happiness, I entrusted him to the envoy from Siltvelt…”

I explained the circumstances—that he had likely been killed at the border of Melromarc. Since I’d already provided context based on what happened when I went to Siltvelt earlier, Father seemed to accept it without hesitation.
“Well, that makes sense. It’s a very inconvenient situation… So last time, you broke through there and went to the country of Siltvelt, right?”
“That’s correct.”
“Then why didn’t you tell me almost anything this time… or rather, why did you only tell me weird stories?”
“What do you mean by ‘weird stories’?”
“Like my future wife being a man, or having a bird’s child.”
“Well… those are events that happened before I entered the loop.”
“What do you mean?”
I bow my head deeply. Yes, no matter how much I apologize, the sins I’ve committed will never be erased.
“Motoyasu-kun?”
“When Father was falsely accused, the place where Itsuki stood—the one that blamed you alongside the Crimson Swine—was actually me.”

“After that, my father was driven out, penniless and with no one on his side. Through steady, painstaking effort, he accomplished the great feat of proving his innocence and succeeded in destroying Trash and this country’s religion.”
“You’re jumping all over the place! I can’t find any part where you’re actually telling a strange story!”
“After that, my father, believing he couldn’t trust pigs, slept with a man as his bodyguard.”
“So what about the daughter?”
“It’s Filolial-sama—Filo-tan—whom my father raised.”
Hearing my words, my father slumped in disappointment and immediately spoke up.
“She’s not his biological child!? And since she’s a monster, that means she’s a pet, right! If you put it that way, people are bound to get the wrong idea!”
My father said, looking utterly exasperated.
